text.p: A university professor who died from wounds received in an attack by robbers in Kazakhstan is a revolutionary martyr, the Shanghai city government has declared.

The Wen Hui Bao newspaper said on Tuesday that Gao Ruhe was beaten by three robbers the night of February 27, 1995, while on the way to his apartment in the Kazakhstan capital of Almaty, where he was a translator for the Shanghai Tea Import and Export Co.
The robbers dragged Gao and another Chinese employee to a rubbish dump, held a gun to Gao's head and demanded the keys to his office and apartment, it said.
Gao, in his 40s, refused to hand over the keys and, in fighting off the robbers, was seriously wounded, it said. He died the next evening.
After a lengthy investigation, the Shanghai government has declared Gao a "revolutionary martyr" who sacrificed his life defending the property of his country and his company, it said.
At the time, Gao's office contained $5,000, a fax machine, samples and valuable equipment. His apartment had goods worth 450,000 yuan ($54,000) and some cash, the newspaper said without elaborating.
It did not explain the delay in reporting the death.

A Fudan University official said Gao had been a deputy professor and teacher of Russian at the university for many years and had been lent to the tea company as an interpreter. He left a wife and two children, she said, but gave no more details.
